scope: Read-only review of system composition, additive module profiles and remaining domain boundaries

resolvedFindings.issue: Strict profile validation in the shared document-type reader would reject an existing or future project before local planner diagnostics
resolvedFindings.resolution: The read-time project type validator no longer validates profiles; new definition and native template write boundaries validate explicitly. Unknown profile data survives read and migration.

checkedBoundaries: Seven modules register fixed version-1 contributions; project profiles request capabilities and never load paths or code.
Required and optional requests are additive. Missing 3D or Rust behavior capabilities never become Scene2D requests and never unmount the document editor.
Scene document types with prose parsing remain ordinary document definitions; representation recognition stays with the existing explicit scene format validators.

Browser composition mounts existing views once and privately stores controllers. Per-domain options are injected separately; the optional media export service exposes a function rather than a sibling controller.
World and build availability intersect module composition with host capability booleans. Module active and profile satisfied do not authorize save, semantic writes or tool execution.
Source callbacks remain in the document runtime; module assembly and metadata refresh do not invoke ordinary Save or expose source text, controllers or callbacks in snapshots.
Refresh of project profiles changes requests and local diagnostics without hot loading, disposing existing controllers or replacing the source authority.
Explicit null, undefined and future-schema profile declarations produce local diagnostics; absence retains legacy behavior.
The exported getStudioSystemSnapshot accessor returns only the detached system DTO, or null before boot; it exposes no source, controllers, callbacks, ports or save authority.

remainingCouplings.limit: The main runtime still owns selection, source baselines, dirty state, document history and ordinary Save. This slice declares its module but does not extract that lifecycle into a replacement kernel.

Scene previews, build planning, runtime selection, control and reports remain assembled within one existing build controller. Contributions describe this current surface, not independent dynamically replaceable executors.
World query, semantic edit forms and creation flows still share their existing world controller and host write gates.

Existing controllers still use their existing DOM and HTTP/platform imports. Domain ports isolate editor callbacks and composition; this is not complete transport inversion or a hostile extension sandbox.
Descriptors are trusted declarative data. There is no dynamic code discovery, package installation, hot unload, automatic migration or executable plugin permission grant.
3D, author Rust execution and native Nuis/ns-nova GUI/providers remain unavailable. Existing Scene2D and backend admission rules remain unchanged.

claimsExcluded: Installed desktop or Android device acceptance
All functional areas have migrated into Rust
New 3D or author Rust compilation support
Any capability declaration grants filesystem, process or renderer authority

dataAdmission.descriptorPolicy: Exact versioned keys, bounded plain enumerable JSON data only; no accessor, toJSON, function, hidden property, symbol, custom prototype, sparse array or cycle is admitted.
dataAdmission.note: Budgets reject whole requests; declarations are never silently truncated. Strict writer validation is independent of nonfatal read planning.
